title: Implement complementary split transient softener
description:
Create Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.h and Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.cpp implementing the repeat transient softener that rounds pick attacks in the feedback loop without coloring the signal at zero amount.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/RepeatToneProcessor.h (produced by d.1; reuse its RBJ high-pass biquad rather than duplicating the coefficient math)
- Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h and Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp (prepare/reset/process conventions, channel count handling)

Required design (the complementary-subtraction identity is binding):
- Extract the high band with a single RBJ high-pass: z_high = HPF(z). Derive the low band by subtraction: z_low = z - z_high. This guarantees exact reconstruction at unity gain. Do NOT substitute a Linkwitz-Riley or any other crossover pair without the subtraction identity; a two-independent-filter split is wrong for this task.
- Crossover default 2500 Hz, expert range 1000 Hz to 6000 Hz, clamped on set.
- Envelopes on abs(z_high): fast envelope tau = 1.5 ms, slow envelope tau = 35 ms, each with alpha = exp(-1.0/(tau*Fs)), computed once in prepare() and on sample-rate change only.
- transient = max(0.0f, (fast - slow) / (slow + epsilon)).
- attenuation_dB = -maxAttenuationDb * clamp(transient, 0, 1); gain = 10^(attenuation_dB/20), applied ONLY to the high band.
- Output: z_low + gain * z_high. When the Attack Softening amount is zero, maxAttenuationDb is zero, gain is exactly 1, and the output must equal the input to within floating-point tolerance.
- Attack Softening 0..100% maps linearly to 0..12 dB of maximum high-band attenuation; provide void setAmountPercent (float percent) performing that mapping with clamping to [0, 100].

Real-time contract (binding): no heap allocation, locks, file IO, string construction, GUI calls, buffer resizing, or coefficient-object allocation inside processing methods. Per-channel state is fixed-size and reset in prepare(). Crossover frequency uses multiplicative smoothing (strictly positive) with high-pass coefficients recomputed only at the bounded control rate in updateCoefficients().

Public API to provide (exact names required):
- void prepare (double sampleRate, int maxBlockSize, int numChannels)
- void reset()
- void setCrossoverFrequency (float hz)
- void setAmountPercent (float percent)
- void setMaxAttenuationDb (float db)
- float processSample (int channel, float x)
- void updateCoefficients()
- float getCurrentAttenuationDb (int channel) const (for tests and telemetry only)
- static float computeAttenuationDb (float fastEnv, float slowEnv, float maxAttenuationDb) implementing the transient ratio and mapping as a pure function so tests can verify it directly.

Do not modify DelayVoice or CMakeLists.txt in this task; integration and source registration happen in d.4.
acceptance_criteria: Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.h declares class RepeatTransientSoftener with prepare, reset, setCrossoverFrequency, setAmountPercent, setMaxAttenuationDb, processSample, updateCoefficients, getCurrentAttenuationDb, and static computeAttenuationDb
Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.cpp derives the low band by subtraction (z_low = z - z_high) from a single RBJ high-pass, and never uses two independent crossover filters
Envelope coefficients use alpha = exp(-1/(tau*Fs)) with tau 1.5 ms fast and 35 ms slow, computed in prepare() rather than per sample
computeAttenuationDb implements transient = max(0, (fast - slow)/(slow + epsilon)) and attenuation_dB = -maxAttenuationDb * clamp(transient, 0, 1)
The computed gain 10^(attenuation_dB/20) is applied only to the high band, with output z_low + gain*z_high
setAmountPercent maps 0..100 percent to 0..12 dB maximum high-band attenuation and clamps out-of-range input
Crossover frequency is clamped to 1000..6000 Hz with a 2500 Hz default and uses multiplicative smoothing
No heap allocation, locks, file IO, string construction, or buffer resizing appears in any processing method in Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.cpp
g++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only -I JUCE/modules -I Source Source/DSP/RepeatTransientSoftener.cpp succeeds, or the file compiles as part of the existing CMake target once registered in d.4
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: replace the complementary subtraction split with an independent crossover filter pair
apply the computed gain to the full-band or low-band signal
allocate memory, lock, or resize buffers inside processing methods
reference artist or song names in any source file

allowed: choose internal per-channel envelope state layout
choose whether the high-pass state is stored in this class or delegated to a RepeatToneProcessor instance member
forbidden: introduce a Linkwitz-Riley or other non-subtractive crossover
introduce lookahead or block-based transient detection
change DelayVoice or plugin processor interfaces
add a new DSP framework or third-party library
